park: You park across from {place} with the engine off and a thermos you do not want.
You find a spot with a clear line to {place}, turn the lights off, and let the car cool around you.
The car ticks as it cools. {place} sits across the way, doing nothing at all, which is what you came to watch.
You settle down in the front seat opposite {place}, the notebook on your knee and the engine silent.
arrived: {n} comes up the path at {t}, key already in hand.
At {t} {n} turns in at {place}, head down against nothing.
{n} arrives at {t} and does not look at the street, which is itself a way of looking.
A door at {place} opens at {t} and {n} goes in, quick and quiet.
left: {n} leaves at {t} and walks away without a backward glance.
At {t} {n} comes out of {place}, pulls the door shut, and tries the handle twice.
{n} is out of the door at {t}, buttoning a coat on the step.
{n} slips out at {t} and takes the long way round the block.
unseen_in: Somebody goes in at about {t}. The light is too poor to say who.
At about {t} a figure turns in at {place}. Hat, coat, no face you could swear to.
unseen_out: A door closes at about {t}, and someone is gone down the dark side of the street before you can see them.
At about {t} a figure comes out of {place} and is lost in the shadow of the hedge.
kept: No one comes or goes. The lamp in the front room stays on, and a shadow crosses it twice.
The curtains do not move. Whoever is inside stays inside for the whole of your watch.
The house keeps itself to itself. A radio plays low behind the glass, and nobody leaves.
quiet: Nothing moves. A cat crosses the road twice and a clock somewhere strikes the hour.
Nobody comes, nobody goes. You write down that nobody comes or goes, because that is what watching is.
The street gives you nothing but a bicycle and a dog. You write down both.
bundle: At {t} {n} comes out with a bundle wrapped in a sheet and carries it round the back of the house.
{n} leaves at {t} carrying something heavy in a coat, walking the way people walk when they want to look as if they are not carrying anything.
spotted: The curtain at the front window moves and does not settle. You have been seen.
A porch light snaps on. Whoever is behind it is looking straight at your car.
Someone stands at an upstairs window for a long minute. Then the blind comes down. You have been seen.
A dog starts up, then a man's voice, then a face at the glass that knows the shape of your car.
tired: Your eyes burn. You have started to see movement in things that are not moving.
Hours in a parked car make a person into a part of it. You are stiff, and cold, and a little less patient than you were.
The thermos is empty and so is the notebook page. You wonder how anyone does this for a living.
figures: someone tall in a dark coat
a figure with a hat pulled low
someone small and quick in a pale scarf
a broad shape under an umbrella
someone in a long cardigan, walking slowly
a figure in work boots and a canvas jacket
